points: Q3 2026 results on Oct 20 will show whether Q2's 12.2% revenue growth and 18.5% adjusted EPS growth are carrying into the second half; a beat and raised FY1 guidance would push the 90-day revenue revision above +0.5% and create a long, while a miss and cuts would push it below -0.5% and create a short.

Q2 recurring subscription Run Rate growth was 8.1% with 95.3% retention, and Q3 must confirm this core book is stable because it underpins the premium valuation. Sustained or better Run Rate growth and retention support a long; deterioration supports a short.

Asset-based fees rose 26.6% in Q2 and added $190.9 million to Run Rate; Q3 will reveal whether that momentum is market-driven or structural, and whether it can justify the 29.1x forward P/E. Continued strong asset-based fee growth supports a long; a sharp slowdown supports a short.

Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin was 62.1%, and reports suggest expenses weighed on the 2026 outlook; Q3 margin trajectory and cost guidance will decide if FY2's 14.4% EPS growth is credible. Margin expansion supports a long; compression or rising cost guidance supports a short.

Capital returns matter for EPS growth: $147.2 million of buybacks through July 20 and a $2.05 quarterly dividend; Q3 commentary on buyback pace and dividend policy will shape FY1/FY2 expectations. A maintained or accelerated return program supports a long; any pullback supports a short.

Peer prints from CBOE, ICE, DFIN and VIRT in late October will provide a post-MSCI read on data/exchange demand; broad strength would reinforce a long case, while broad weakness would reinforce a short case.
watch: Organic recurring subscription Run Rate growth vs Q2's 8.1%: above supports a long, at or below supports a short.
Adjusted EBITDA margin vs Q2's 62.1%: expansion supports a long, contraction supports a short.
Asset-based fee revenue growth vs Q2's 26.6%: above supports a long, a material slowdown supports a short.
90-day revenue estimate revision (rev90): crosses above +0.5% creates a long, crosses below -0.5% creates a short.
